items.title: Amazon Connect Customer automatically saves in-progress emails as drafts
items.content_snippet: Amazon Connect Customer automatically saves in-progress emails as drafts, helping agents resume work without losing progress when connectivity is interrupted or when their browser is accidentally closed or refreshed. When agents return, their drafts are restored with the message body, recipients, subject line, and attachment references intact. Customers can also access saved draft data in their Amazon S3 buckets to build integrations with other applications.

items.title: Amazon CloudFront now provides viewer ISP and post-quantum TLS details
items.content_snippet: Amazon CloudFront can now forward two new optional headers to your origin. The CloudFront-Viewer-ISP header contains the name of the viewer's internet service provider (ISP), so you can see which network a request came from. The CloudFront-Viewer-TLS-Details header describes the cryptography used on each viewer's TLS connection, so you can see whether a connection used post-quantum cryptography (PQC). items.content_snippet: Amazon MSK now supports version 1.3 of Transport Layer Security (TLS) protocol for MSK Provisioned clusters through encryption policies. TLS 1.3 delivers faster, more secure encryption for streaming data and is increasingly required by compliance frameworks and enterprise security standards. It is also one of the prerequisites for post-quantum cryptography for protecting data against attacks that collect encrypted traffic now with the intent to decrypt it later.
